title: Evaluation of the Validity of Cervical Ultrasonography Compared with Computed Tomography in the Assessment of Cervical Lymph Node Status in Patients with Head and Neck Cancer.
summary:
In patients with head and neck cancer, it is important to determine whether the cancer has spread to the lymph nodes in the neck. Before surgery, this is usually assessed using ultrasound and/or computed tomography (CT). However, the presence of cancer cells in the lymph nodes can only be confirmed after the lymph nodes have been surgically removed and examined under a microscope.

This study will analyze existing medical records from patients who underwent treatment at the Department of Otorhinolaryngology between 2017 and 2025. The aim is to compare how accurately ultrasound and CT predict the presence of lymph node metastases before surgery and to determine which imaging method provides the most reliable assessment.

Only data that have already been collected as part of routine clinical care will be used. No additional examinations, procedures, or interventions will be performed for this study. All data will be pseudonymized before analysis to protect participants' privacy.
conditions: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

interventions.name: Retrospective data collection and study. All patients who underwent neck dissection at the Department of Otorhinolaryngology (ENT) between 2017 and 2025 will be included in the study. We expect approximately 600 cases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who underwent neck dissection as part of the treatment for head and neck cancer at University Medical Center Mannheim between 2017 and 2025.
Exclusion criteria:
none
